DVDs were first released in Japan in late 1996: according to Wikipedia, DVD-Video became available there on October 19, 1996, with major releases beginning December 20, 1996 [d4]. Britannica confirms that the first DVD players went on sale in Japan in 1996, after competing technology groups agreed on a common format by end of 1995 [d9]. The DVD specification (version 1.0) was finalized in September 1996 [d7][d2]. DVDs then launched in the United States in March 1997 [d4][d7], with the US debut timed to coincide with the Academy Awards ceremony [d5][d6]. Early US DVD releases included titles such as Twister, Blade Runner, Eraser, and Goodfellas [d8][d5]. By the early 2000s, DVDs had largely replaced VHS tapes as the dominant home entertainment format [d5][d3].
